ticker.text: ▲ CANADA CONFIRMS 10TH HANTAVIRUS CASE: YUKON RESIDENT IN 70S HOSPITALIZED VICTORIA
▲ WHO DON601: 11 CASES (8 CONFIRMED ANDV, 2 PROBABLE, 1 INCONCLUSIVE) — 3 DEATHS
► 6 HONDIUS PAX — 5 AUSTRALIANS, 1 NZ — IN BULLSBROOK QUARANTINE NEAR PERTH WA
► CRITICALLY ILL FRENCH WOMAN ON ECMO ARTIFICIAL LUNG AT BICHAT HOSPITAL PARIS
► 2 US PAX MONITORED EMORY UNIV HOSPITAL ATLANTA; CDC: NO PUBLIC RISK TO AMERICANS
▲ ANDES STRAIN MATCHES SOUTH AMERICAN STRAINS; NO NEW MUTATIONS DETECTED — AP
► HONDIUS EN ROUTE ROTTERDAM FOR FULL DISINFECTION; ARCTIC SCHEDULE UNCERTAIN
▲ WHO: EU/EEA + GLOBAL GENERAL POPULATION RISK VERY LOW; MONITORING ONGOING
// ILLINOIS RESIDENT HANTAVIRUS CASE ASSESSED UNRELATED TO MV HONDIUS OUTBREAK
► PHAC CONFIRMS POSITIVE HANTAVIRUS AMONG FOUR CANADIAN HONDIUS RETURNEES 17 MAY

sites.name: M/V HONDIUS
sites.desc: WHO DON601 (13 May) confirms 11 total cases: 8 laboratory-confirmed Andes virus, 2 probable, 1 inconclusive pending further testing; 3 deaths. No new cases or deaths since previous update; crew remains asymptomatic. Vessel evacuated at Granadilla de Abona; en route Rotterdam with skeleton crew of 30 + Dutch nurse for full disinfection.

sites.name: USHUAIA / ARGENTINA ROUTE
sites.desc: Index case (Dutch male, 70, died 11 Apr) took 4-month road trip 27 Nov 2025–1 Apr 2026 through Chile, Uruguay, Argentina before boarding; Dutch couple believed to have contracted virus during South America visit pre-boarding per AP 13 May. AP News 17 May confirms Andes strain matches known South American strains with no new mutations; Malbrán Institute trapping/testing rodents along route.

sites.name: SAINT HELENA
sites.desc: 30 passengers disembarked 24 Apr including Dutch index male's body and Dutch widow (later died Johannesburg) and Swiss confirmed male. UKHSA contact-tracing 30 disembarkees plus 82 pax and 6 crew from 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight.

sites.name: JOHANNESBURG
sites.desc: Case 2 (Dutch widow, 69, PCR+) died Johannesburg hospital 26 Apr — confirmed Andes virus fatality. Case 3 (British guide Martin Anstee, 56, PCR+) treated at Johannesburg ICU; improving, transferred Netherlands. A second British national confirmed PCR-positive 08 May in a South Africa health facility.

sites.name: AMSTERDAM / NIJMEGEN / ROTTERDAM
sites.desc: British Case 3 (Anstee) transferred to Netherlands after improving in South Africa. Dutch crew member (41, confirmed) treated at Radboud UMC Nijmegen. Netherlands lab PCR-confirmed German woman died of Andes virus; MV Hondius sailing to Rotterdam for full disinfection.

sites.name: MANCHESTER / WIRRAL / LONDON
sites.desc: 22 British nationals evacuated Tenerife; 20 flew Titan Airways charter to Manchester, now at Arrowe Park Hospital (Wirral) for up to 72-hr clinical assessment + testing, then 45-day self-isolation. UKHSA: 3 British cases total — 2 PCR-confirmed (SA/NL) + 1 suspected Tristan da Cunha.

sites.name: PARIS / LE BOURGET
sites.desc: France confirmed first hantavirus case: one of five repatriated Hondius passengers tested PCR-positive; critically ill French woman on ECMO artificial lung at Bichat Hospital Paris. AP News 17 May confirms Andes virus detected matches known South American strains with no new mutations indicating increased transmissibility or severity; French government mandated 42-day quarantine with 22 potential contact cases identified across international flights.

sites.name: ZURICH / GENEVA
sites.desc: PCR-confirmed male passenger disembarked St Helena 24 Apr; symptoms onset 01 May, tested positive Andes virus 05 May at University Hospital Zurich. Illumina sequencing confirmed Andes variant with high similarity to Argentina 2018–19 strains and no new mutations; wife asymptomatic and isolating.

sites.name: BERLIN / DÜSSELDORF
sites.desc: German woman died on board 02 May (fever/malaise onset 28 Apr, pneumonia); Netherlands postmortem PCR confirmed Andes virus. German nationals repatriated via Dutch charter from Tenerife 10 May. RKI contact tracing active; asymptomatic 65-year-old German contact tested NEGATIVE.

sites.name: ALICANTE
sites.desc: 32-year-old woman (seated 2 rows behind deceased Dutch woman on 25 Apr Airlink flight) returned first PCR NEGATIVE at Centro Nacional de Microbiología. Awaiting second confirmatory PCR; if also negative, transfers to Gómez Ulla Military Hospital Madrid.

sites.name: TENERIFE
sites.desc: Hondius docked Granadilla de Abona port 10 May concluding 40-day health crisis; 152 disembarked in successful 23-nation evacuation praised by WHO. One Spanish passenger tested PCR-positive post-disembarkation (12 May, El País); patient asymptomatic, confirmatory PCR pending.

sites.name: MADRID
sites.desc: Spanish nationals were the first nationality evacuated from Tenerife per AP News, landing Torrejón de Ardoz military airport and transported to Gómez Ulla Military Hospital. No Spanish nationals showing symptoms at disembarkation; PCR on arrival + Day 7 with twice-daily temperature monitoring.

sites.name: BARCELONA
sites.desc: Two Barcelona contacts monitored: (1) South African woman (asymptomatic flight contact of Dutch deceased) spent ~1 week here before returning South Africa — confirmed asymptomatic. (2) Barcelona-resident woman identified 09 May as flight contact after mid-flight seat change; asymptomatic, under official monitoring per Spanish Health Ministry.

sites.name: TRISTAN DA CUNHA
sites.desc: UKHSA confirmed suspected case 08 May: British male islander aboard Hondius during 13–15 Apr stop; symptoms onset 28 Apr, stable in isolation on island. RAF A400M emergency airdrop 09 May: 6 paratroopers + 2 military clinicians parachuted onto island's golf course delivering 3.3 tonnes medical supplies — first-ever UK military humanitarian parachute deployment.

sites.name: SINGAPORE
sites.desc: CLEARED 09 May: Both male residents (aged 67 and 65) tested NEGATIVE for hantavirus including Andes virus via multiple PCR samples — Singapore CDA confirmed. Both had disembarked Hondius at St Helena and traveled on 25 Apr Airlink flight; monitoring continues through full incubation window.

sites.name: VICTORIA / BRITISH COLUMBIA
sites.desc: PHAC confirmed one positive hantavirus case among four Canadian Hondius returnees (AP News, 17 May): Yukon resident in their 70s hospitalized in Victoria with fever and headache, marking the 10th confirmed case linked to the outbreak. Confirmatory PCR sent to National Microbiology Lab Winnipeg; partner tested negative. Dr. Bonnie Henry reassured no increased risk to general public.

sites.name: ONTARIO
sites.desc: Two Ontario residents self-isolating — Hondius passengers who returned home early, asymptomatic. Canadian repatriation flight departed Tenerife 10 May per AP News (second nationality after Spain to evacuate). PHAC coordinating monitoring per 07 May government statement.

sites.name: QUEBEC
sites.desc: One Quebec resident self-isolating — not a Hondius passenger but shared homebound flight with two Canadian Hondius disembarkees. Asymptomatic; PHAC monitoring active.

sites.name: ARIZONA
sites.desc: ADHS monitoring one returning passenger under 42-day observation. Asymptomatic as of 17 May. CDC notified ADHS 05 May; public risk assessed as very low per CDC Newsroom 08 May. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort across 6 states.

sites.name: CALIFORNIA
sites.desc: CDPH monitoring one returned Hondius traveler via daily temperature checks and symptom assessment. A second California resident transited Tenerife to Nebraska NQU via CDC/HHS biocontainment charter. No California residents reported ill as of 17 May.

sites.name: GEORGIA
sites.desc: Two American Hondius passengers transferred to Emory University Hospital SCDU in Atlanta for monitoring per AP News 17 May; CDC chartered a flight to Hartsfield-Jackson for their transport. Health officials emphasize no public risk. Two additional Georgia residents asymptomatic and following CDC guidance at home.

sites.name: TEXAS
sites.desc: Texas DSHS monitoring two returning Hondius passengers. Both asymptomatic as of 17 May. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort across 6 states.

sites.name: VIRGINIA
sites.desc: VDH monitoring one returning Hondius passenger. Asymptomatic. CDC classified response as Level-3; Emergency Operations Center activated. Six states — AZ, CA, GA, TX, VA, NJ — monitoring at least 9 early-disembarkees or contacts.

sites.name: NEW JERSEY
sites.desc: NJ DOH monitoring two individuals potentially exposed to a Hondius passenger post-disembarkation during air travel. Neither symptomatic as of 17 May. Exposure occurred during air travel abroad; residents were not Hondius passengers themselves.

sites.name: NEBRASKA
sites.desc: Two Americans transported to National Quarantine Center at UNMC in biocontainment units; one who tested mildly positive was cleared of virus per AP 15 May. 15 additional passengers quarantined at NQU including content creator Jake Rosmarin. Dr. Stephen Kornfeld (Oregon) released 14 May after inconclusive swabs resolved negative; CDC confirmed no further US cases as of 17 May and risk to American public remains extremely low per CDC 14 May update.

sites.name: UTAH
sites.desc: Utah DHHS confirmed at least one Utah resident among the Americans aboard MV Hondius. Person asymptomatic; disembarked Tenerife with federal escort to Nebraska NQU for evaluation. No Utah residents monitored at home as of 17 May.

sites.name: ILLINOIS
sites.desc: Winnebago County resident feared to have contracted hantavirus (non-Andes variant) after cleaning a rodent-infested property per The Daily Beast 14 May. Case assessed as unrelated to MV Hondius outbreak; showing mild symptoms, not hospitalized, and recovering.

sites.name: MANILA
sites.desc: 38 Filipino crew members aboard Hondius; Philippines DOH confirmed none currently ill as of 17 May. Skeleton crew of ~30 (predominantly Filipino) will remain aboard to sail vessel to Rotterdam with Dutch nurse. Monitoring continues through incubation window.

sites.name: DUBLIN / BALDONNELL
sites.desc: Irish passengers repatriated 10 May via Defence Forces Dassault Falcon 6X government jet to Baldonnell — first medevac mission for the aircraft (acquired Dec 2025, €53M). Irish Dept of Health National Incident Management Team stood up; coordinating with ECDC, HSE. No symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: PRAIA
sites.desc: Hondius anchored Praia 03–06 May; refused docking by Cape Verde per The Week. Three medevac patients evacuated 06 May — two flew Amsterdam (hazmat teams at Schiphol), third plane made unscheduled Gran Canaria refueling stop after Morocco refused permission + medical equipment malfunction.

sites.name: COPENHAGEN
sites.desc: Danish Patient Safety Authority confirmed one Danish national was aboard MV Hondius. Person returned to Denmark end of April, self-isolating, no symptoms, not in close contact with any confirmed case. Monitoring active per national protocol.

sites.name: BRUSSELS
sites.desc: Belgian nationals repatriated via Dutch charter from Tenerife (10 May Sunday flight alongside NL/DE/GR nationals) per AP News repatriation sequence. Belgian federal health authorities coordinating with ECDC. No symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: WELLINGTON
sites.desc: One NZ national arrived at Bullsbrook quarantine facility near Perth, Australia for mandatory three-week quarantine per AP 16 May, traveling alongside five Australians on RAAF Base Pearce intake flight; all tested negative before departure. NZ Ministry of Health coordinating contact tracing; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: STOCKHOLM
sites.desc: Sweden confirmed among 12+ countries monitoring Hondius nationals who disembarked. Swedish Public Health Agency (Folkhälsomyndigheten) coordinating; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: ANKARA
sites.desc: Turkish nationals evacuated Tenerife 10 May per AP News multi-nation repatriation sequence. Turkish Ministry of Health coordinating; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: BASSETERRE
sites.desc: Saint Kitts and Nevis confirmed among 12+ countries monitoring nationals who disembarked MV Hondius. Local health authorities monitoring; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: ATHENS
sites.desc: Greek nationals repatriated via Dutch charter from Tenerife (10 May Sunday flight alongside NL/DE/BE nationals). Greek Ministry of Health coordinating with ECDC; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: WARSAW
sites.desc: Polish nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing. Polish Chief Sanitary Inspectorate coordinating with ECDC; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: LISBON
sites.desc: Portuguese nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per ECDC briefing. DGS Portugal coordinating with ECDC; no symptomatic cases reported.

sites.name: PERTH / BULLSBROOK / SYDNEY
sites.desc: Five Australians and one New Zealander arrived at RAAF Base Pearce near Perth 16 May and transported to Bullsbrook quarantine facility for mandatory three-week quarantine per AP 16 May; all tested negative before departure. Health Minister Mark Butler enacted one of the world's strictest quarantine responses citing 42-day incubation risk; facility largely unused since COVID-19 pandemic.
